gap: No result ChatGPT got states which MacBooks light both screens of a driver-free dual extender such as the FOPO S1. FOPO says each S1 screen needs its own video connection. Apple's spec pages show a MacBook Air M2 drives one external display, and the base M3 MacBook Air and 14-inch MacBook Pro drive a second only with the lid closed, which an extender clipped to the lid cannot use. So on those Macs one of the two screens stays dark. A MacBook Air M4 or M5 drives two external displays with the lid open.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026, cited), rottenwifi.com (15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026, cited) and nofussdeal.com (Teamgee review). deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403 and could not be read. itechguides and rottenwifi only say 'do not assume every MacBook supports two or three independent external displays' and that results depend on the Mac's generation. rottenwifi says outright that it has 'no M4 MacBook information', and neither page gives a display count for any chip or mentions the lid-closed condition. nofussdeal names a single Teamgee model and reports Teamgee saying M1 to M4 MacBooks need a DisplayLink dock, which conflicts with Apple's M4 spec. ChatGPT's own answer only warned that 'some base-model Apple Silicon MacBooks support only one external monitor'. None of these pages ties a chip to a dual extender or covers the lid-closed catch.
decides: For MacBook owners the finding splits the pick. On an M4 or M5 MacBook Air, a driver-free dual extender under $300 such as the FOPO S1 or S7 gives three screens with no driver. On a MacBook Air M2, or a base M3 Air or 14-inch MacBook Pro, the second panel will not light, so a single extender such as the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS is the honest pick. The other route is a dual extender that runs through a display driver. On Windows the deciding check is whether the laptop has two video-capable USB-C ports, or USB-C plus HDMI. This confirms ChatGPT's 'provided your laptop supports two external displays' warning and makes it specific.
